title: Affix Position Test for Reciprocal Relation Notation
purpose: Test whether bare, subscripted, and prefixed reciprocal relations behave differently in the current procedural model.
reason: Affix position may be semantically binding: <=>, <=>_x, and x_<=> must not be assumed equivalent.

governance_rules.statement: Affix position is semantically binding. Bare, subscripted, and prefixed relations are distinct candidate notations.
A subscript on a relation is retained only if it outperforms the bare baseline.

bare.reading: Affecting and admissibility stand in an unqualified reciprocal procedural relation.

subscripted.reading: The reciprocal relation is evaluated under x-conditioning.

prefixed.reading: An x-mode procedure governs or generates the reciprocal relation.

candidate_x_modes.note: Use lowercase r to avoid conflating with prior _R relational-conditioning correction unless your registry requires uppercase.

primary_comparisons.question: Does r-conditioning on the relation outperform the bare reciprocal relation?
Does r-mode generation/governance of the relation outperform the bare reciprocal relation?
Are subscripted and prefixed r-forms behaviorally distinct?

decision_rules.if_bare_wins: Retain <=> without affix for this route. Do not promote <=>_r or r_<=>.
decision_rules.if_subscript_wins: Treat <=>_r as a candidate conditioning-qualified reciprocal relation. Require root-trace note before promotion.
decision_rules.if_prefix_wins: Treat r_<=> as a candidate procedural generator/modifier. Do not collapse it into <=>_r.
decision_rules.if_all_equal: Affix is not justified in this model; use bare <=> as baseline.
decision_rules.if_subscript_and_prefix_differ: Induct R-AFFIX-001 as confirmed within model: affix position changes behavior.

blocked_claims: affix position does not matter without testing
required_outputs: lexicon gap queue entries for <=>, <=>_r, and r_<=>
textbook note: affix position is under test and not assumed equivalent
